tldr: The paper introduces GUI-Reflection, an automatic framework that integrates self-reflection and error correction capabilities into end-to-end multimodal GUI models across pre-training, offline supervised fine-tuning, and online training stages.
contributions: GUI-Reflection Task Suite for explicitly training and evaluating reflection-oriented abilities during GUI pre-training
A scalable automatic data pipeline to construct reflection and error correction scenarios from existing successful trajectories without manual annotation
An online learning environment for mobile GUI agents and an iterative online reflection tuning algorithm
methods: The framework decomposes reflection and error correction into three atomic capabilities: action verification, action reversal, and mistake-informed reattempt, trained during GUI pre-training via the GUI-Reflection Task Suite. For offline SFT, an automatic data pipeline generates reflection/correction scenarios by either modifying task goals to induce incorrect actions or inserting ineffective incorrect actions into successful trajectories. For online training, a distributed Android-based environment with 215 task templates across 11 apps supports an iterative reflection tuning algorithm that collects rollouts, annotates pre-error correction and post-error correction actions using MLLMs, and dynamically adjusts task sampling weights based on success rates with a curriculum learning strategy.
results: Paper text is truncated before the experiments/results section, so specific quantitative findings are not available in the provided text.
limitations: Relies on MLLM-based automatic annotation which may introduce errors
The MLLM-based verifier for task evaluation may be less accurate than programmatic verification
Evaluation focuses on Android-based mobile tasks
Reflection capability quality depends on the base MLLM's original abilities, which offline SFT may inadvertently diminish
